name: CT-04
label: Safe D

key_factors: Himes incumbency with large financial advantage
Prediction markets price Himes near certain
model.rationale: Himes is a well-funded incumbent in a D+13 district, while Goldstein has raised only about $47,000, and markets price his win odds near zero. Nothing in the evidence suggests anything other than a safe Democratic hold.
model.watch: A late, unexpected influx of outside spending against Himes or a major scandal would be the only realistic path to narrowing this race.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Jim Himes seeks another term in a southwestern Connecticut district that leans Democratic by about 13 points. He enters the general election with roughly $2.5 million on hand after raising nearly $1.4 million, while Republican Michael Goldstein has raised under $50,000 and has no outside support on either side. An independent candidate also appears on the ballot but shows no measurable campaign activity.

Prediction markets give Himes about a 96 percent chance of winning, and no expert raters flag the race as competitive. With no public polling available, the outlook rests on the district's partisan lean, Himes's incumbency, and the lopsided financial picture, all of which point to a comfortable Democratic hold.
